mechaber.en:
The law if the courtyards did not establish an eruv together and also did not partner in the alleyway. Containing 1 section. If
the courtyards did not make an eruv together and also did not make a partnership in the alleyway, it is permitted to carry throughout the entire alleyway items that rested in it on Shabbat—whether the courtyards made an eruv with the houses or they did not make an eruv. According to our teacher Rabbi Moshe bar Maimon, this applies specifically when they did not make an eruv of courtyards with the houses. But if they made an eruv of courtyards with the houses, one may only carry in the alleyway within four cubits.

mishnah_berurah.he:
(א) אם לא עירבו וכו' - ר"ל אף אם לא עירבו וכו' דאם עירבו הרי הוא ג"כ כעין שיתוף מבוי וכבסימן הקודם:
(ב) כלים ששבתו בתוכו - וה"ה דמותר להוציא מחצר למבוי כלים ששבתו בתוכו וכן מן המבוי לחצר וכדלעיל בסימן שע"ב ס"א דלא תקנו חכמים שיתופי מבואות אלא להתיר להוציא למבוי כלים ששבתו בבית אבל לענין חצרות ומבואות עצמן לא תקנו ורשות אחד הוא דמותר לטלטל מזה לזה וכן שוין הם גם בזה דכמו דמותר לטלטל בכל החצר כלים ששבתו בתוכו אף אם לא עירבו עם הבתים כן מותר לטלטל בכל המבוי אף אם לא נשתתפו בני החצרות עם המבוי ופשוט דכ"ז מיירי שהיה המבוי עצמו מתוקן בלחי וקורה כדין:
(ג) בין עירבו חצרות וכו' - דמצויין כלי הבית בחצר ושייך למגזר דלמא אתי לאפוקי כלי הבית למבוי אפ"ה שרי:
(ד) ולהרב רבינו משה בר מיימון וכו' - ולהלכה נקטינן כדעה הראשונה ואפילו להרמב"ם דוקא כשהמבוי מתוקן בלחי וקורה אבל אם הוא מתוקן בצורת הפתח גם לדידיה מותר בכולו [אחרונים]:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(1) If they did not make an eruv, etc. Meaning, even if they did not make an eruv. If they did, the eruv itself functions somewhat like a shituf mevo'ot, as explained in the preceding siman.
(2) Utensils that rested within it. The same law applies that one may carry from a courtyard to an alley utensils that rested in the courtyard, and from the alley to a courtyard, as explained above in siman 372, seif 1.
The Sages instituted shitufei mevo'ot only to permit bringing into the alley utensils that had rested inside houses. With respect to the courtyards and alleys themselves, they did not institute a prohibition. They are one domain, and one may carry from one to another.
They are also alike in this respect: just as one may carry throughout an entire courtyard utensils that rested there even if the residents did not make an eruv with the houses, so too one may carry throughout an entire alley utensils that rested there even if the residents of the courtyards did not make a shituf with the alley.
It is obvious that all this assumes that the alley itself was properly rectified with a lechi or korah.
(3) Whether the courtyards made eruvin, etc. Even though household utensils are commonly found in the courtyard and one might have decreed lest a person come to carry household utensils into the alley, nevertheless it is permitted.
(4) And according to Rambam, etc. As a matter of halakhah we follow the first opinion. Even according to Rambam, his restriction applies specifically when the alley is rectified by a lechi or korah; if it is rectified with a tzurat hapetach, he too agrees that carrying throughout it is permitted. [Later authorities.]

kaf_hachayyim.he: א) [סעיף א'] אם לא עירבו החצירות יחד ר"ל אף אם עירבו כל החצירות ביחד דאם עירבו כל החצירות דרך פתחים ביחד בלא"ה שרי דהו"ל כמו שיתוף כמ"ש בסי' הקודם:
kaf_hachayyim.en: 1) [Se'if 1] If the courtyards did not establish an eruv together. This means even if the residents of each courtyard established an eruv among themselves. If all the courtyards established a single eruv together through entrances between them, carrying is permitted in any event, since that eruv is equivalent to a shituf, as stated in the preceding siman.
